classification.difficultyReason: Recognise a square in a radical involving sqrt(x), retain its restricted domain, and reflect the negative portion of the base graph.

inlines.text: upwards, preserving the sharp point at

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{x}-1)^2}\\y&=|\sqrt{x}-1|\end{align*}$$
The inner square root requires $x\ge0$. Sketch $y=\sqrt{x}-1$, which starts at $(0,-1)$ and crosses the x-axis at $(1,0)$. Reflect the portion for $0\le x<1$ across the x-axis. The graph starts at $(0,1)$, decreases to the sharp minimum $(1,0)$, then increases without bound. Domain: $[0,\infty)$; range: $[0,\infty)$.

spec.mathematics: y=1-sqrt(x) for 0<=x<=1; y=sqrt(x)-1 for x>=1. Parametric plotting uses x=t^2 and y=|t-1| for t>=0.
